source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: I would like to proceed with the 12-page sample from you. Please tell me if you want to accept, and I will send over the contract. Its terms will be what we discussed in our messages. Let me know if you have any questions; if not, I will send it shortly. Thanks!

value_updates.script_format: panel format for each comic page

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
A quick update: I made solid progress today and developed a provisional breakdown that reaches Tom's meeting with Apollonia on comic page 12. I may determine that the pacing is too fast if some beats require additional room to breathe, but that is something I will have to assess while working.
There are two questions—or, more accurately, two possible approaches to the script—that I would like to confirm with you:
1. In several spots, I am considering adapting portions of the scene descriptions into "voice over" captions.
2. To save page space and improve efficiency, I may omit a few brief exchanges. One example is at the bottom of page 23, when Carter tells Tom that he is invited to the dinner Tom attends in the next scene.
Before doing so, I wanted to ask whether departures from the script on that scale are acceptable, or whether you want the comic to follow the screenplay line-for-line. Please share your thoughts.
Thanks.

ambiguity.description: It is unresolved whether the sample must follow the screenplay line-for-line or may use voice-over captions and omit minor exchanges for pacing.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
In that event, thank you very much. At that rate, I can devote more time to determining the strongest way to present all of the material instead of adhering so closely to the screenplay.

Do you want me to begin next week, or should I hold off until you say "go?"

I can commit to writing 80-85 comic pages. After reviewing the next two episodes and the novel, I will decide how much of the story can fit within that length. While doing so, should I structure the pacing around eventually scripting the remainder of the story? In other words, do you want this portion to feel self-contained, or should it emphasize leaving readers wondering, "What's next?"

Thanks,
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]

ambiguity.description: The amount of story to cover and whether the volume should be self-contained or end as an open continuation remain unresolved.
